# plugins/ — plugin kinds, compat contract, in-tree policy

Applies on top of the root `AGENTS.md`. Authoring guide + canonical compat contract:
`website/docs/developer-guide/plugins/index.md`. Per-kind guides: `memory-provider-plugin.md`,
`model-provider-plugin.md`, `context-engine-plugin.md`, `image-gen-provider-plugin.md`, ...

## Plugins never touch core (Teknium, May 2026)

Plugins live in their own directory and work within the ABCs / hooks / `ctx` surface we provide.
A plugin MUST NOT modify `run_agent.py`, `cli.py`, `gateway/run.py`, `hermes_cli/main.py`, etc.
If it needs a capability the framework lacks, widen the **generic** plugin surface (new hook, new
ctx method) and have the plugin use it — never hardcode plugin-specific logic into core (PR #5295
removed 95 lines of hardcoded honcho argparse from `main.py`). Plugin setup goes through
`hermes memory setup` → `provider.post_setup(hermes_home, config)`, never a parallel top-level
command. A hook with no concrete consumer is speculative infrastructure and is rejected (root).

## What may live in this tree (policy)

- **No new in-tree memory providers (May 2026).** `plugins/memory/` is closed (honcho, mem0,
  supermemory, byterover, holographic, openviking, retaindb stay; bug fixes welcome; hindsight moved
  to the plugin catalog in Sep 2026 — `plugin-catalog/hindsight.yaml`, auto-installed by
  `hermes_cli/memory_provider_migration.py` for homes still configured for it). New
  backends ship as standalone repos implementing the same `MemoryProvider` ABC, discovered through
  the same path, integrated via `hermes memory setup` / `post_setup()`.
- **No new third-party-product plugins (June 2026).** Observability/metrics backends, vendor SaaS
  connectors, analytics dashboards, paid-service tie-ins ship as standalone plugin repos
  (`~/.hermes/plugins/` or pip entry point) promoted in Discord `#plugins-skills-and-skins`. Reason:
  every absorbed product is our maintenance burden against a fast-moving core for a backend we don't
  own. `observability/`, `kanban/`, `disk-cleanup/` are precedent, not an invitation. Closing such a
  PR is a coupling decision, not a quality judgment.
- Reference/docs-companion plugins (`example-dashboard`, `strike-freedom-cockpit`,
  `plugin-llm-example`, `plugin-llm-async-example`) live in
  [`hermes-example-plugins`](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-example-plugins), not here.

## Plugin catalog (`plugin-catalog/`, Sep 2026)

The ONLY discovery system for out-of-tree plugins. One YAML per entry, 40-hex SHA pin mandatory,
human-merged via PR (`plugin-catalog/README.md` = admission policy; `plugin-catalog-ci.yml` clones
each changed entry at its pin and runs `hermes plugins validate`). `removed.yaml` is the kill list —
every install path (CLI, dashboard, TUI) refuses matches (repo URLs compared by canonical

installed plugin from the same check at `update`, `enable` and load (`gate_manifest`). Catalog
provenance lives on the installer-owned `.install-metadata.json` record (`catalog` block, sha =
checked-out commit), NEVER in the tree: the in-tree `.hermes-catalog.json` is a convenience copy the

# plugins/ — plugin kinds, compat contract, in-tree policy

Applies on top of the root `AGENTS.md`. Authoring guide + canonical compat contract:
`website/docs/developer-guide/plugins/index.md`. Per-kind guides: `memory-provider-plugin.md`,
`model-provider-plugin.md`, `context-engine-plugin.md`, `image-gen-provider-plugin.md`, ...

## Plugins never touch core (Teknium, May 2026)

Plugins live in their own directory and work within the ABCs / hooks / `ctx` surface we provide.
A plugin MUST NOT modify `run_agent.py`, `cli.py`, `gateway/run.py`, `hermes_cli/main.py`, etc.
If it needs a capability the framework lacks, widen the **generic** plugin surface (new hook, new
ctx method) and have the plugin use it — never hardcode plugin-specific logic into core (PR #5295
removed 95 lines of hardcoded honcho argparse from `main.py`). Plugin setup goes through
`hermes memory setup` → `provider.post_setup(hermes_home, config)`, never a parallel top-level
command. A hook with no concrete consumer is speculative infrastructure and is rejected (root).

## What may live in this tree (policy)

- **No new in-tree memory providers (May 2026).** `plugins/memory/` is closed (honcho, mem0,
  supermemory, byterover, holographic, openviking, retaindb stay; bug fixes welcome; hindsight moved
  to the plugin catalog in Sep 2026 — `plugin-catalog/hindsight.yaml`, auto-installed by
  `hermes_cli/memory_provider_migration.py` for homes still configured for it). New
  backends ship as standalone repos implementing the same `MemoryProvider` ABC, discovered through
  the same path, integrated via `hermes memory setup` / `post_setup()`.
- **No new third-party-product plugins (June 2026).** Observability/metrics backends, vendor SaaS
  connectors, analytics dashboards, paid-service tie-ins ship as standalone plugin repos
  (`~/.hermes/plugins/` or pip entry point) promoted in Discord `#plugins-skills-and-skins`. Reason:
  every absorbed product is our maintenance burden against a fast-moving core for a backend we don't
  own. `observability/`, `kanban/`, `disk-cleanup/` are precedent, not an invitation. Closing such a
  PR is a coupling decision, not a quality judgment.
- Reference/docs-companion plugins (`example-dashboard`, `strike-freedom-cockpit`,
  `plugin-llm-example`, `plugin-llm-async-example`) live in
  [`hermes-example-plugins`](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-example-plugins), not here.

## Plugin catalog (`plugin-catalog/`, Sep 2026)

provenance lives on the installer-owned `.install-metadata.json` record (`catalog` block, sha =
checked-out commit), NEVER in the tree: the in-tree `.hermes-catalog.json` is a convenience copy the
Desktop reads for "Install here"; Python never trusts it (a repo can ship a forged one).

`/docs/api/plugin-catalog.json` published by the docs build, in-tree fallback),
`hermes_cli/plugins_cmd_catalog.py` (resolution, `.hermes-catalog.json` provenance sidecar,

|---|---|---|---|

| Memory provider | `plugins/memory/<name>/` | `plugins/memory/__init__.py`: bundled → `$HERMES_HOME/plugins/` → `./.hermes/plugins/` (opt-in `HERMES_ENABLE_PROJECT_PLUGINS`) → `hermes_agent.memory_providers` entry points; **bundled-first** | Activated by name via `memory.provider`, so a dropped-in dir must not shadow a shipped one (reverse of general later-wins). Enumerates without importing. Compatibility is a **behavior contract**, not a monolithic `PLUGIN_API_VERSION`, a manifest-wide
native `api:` match, or version literals on unrelated payloads. Documented surfaces stay additive:

  signatures receive only the fields they declare and `**kwargs` callbacks get the full payload.
- Never remove or rename `PluginContext` methods; new parameters are optional with defaults and
  keyword-only where possible.
- Unknown native manifest fields are ignored.
- New provider methods get default implementations; optional callback kwargs are
  signature-inspected, not forwarded unconditionally.
- A local schema version exists only for a capability with a wire or persisted contract, and old
  state/config/session replay is preserved or migrated.
- Deprecations: once-per-process warning, documented replacement + migration note, ≥ 2 subsequent
  minor releases before removal.
- Compat tests load **frozen plugins through the real discovery path** and assert outcomes — never
  exact registry/catalog counts, source-reading tests, or "a global version literal changed".

`PLUGIN-COMPAT` `__getattr__` blocks (listed in `COMPAT_MANIFEST.md` / `compat_manifest.json`)
until `hermes_cli.plugin_compat.COMPAT_REMOVAL_DATE`, when the commit that added them is reverted.
`hermes_cli/plugin_compat.py` is the single source: `scan_plugin` (AST scan), `compat_report`

## Tests

`tests/plugins/`. Load through real discovery with a temp `HERMES_HOME`; assert behaviour (tool
registered, hook fired with expected kwargs), not counts. Opt-in telemetry rule applies to plugins
too: no attribution tag ships by default.

def native_runner(workspace, monkeypatch):
    # Retain the real key derivation, run generations, hard interruption and
    # native release path; only platform/plugin I/O is a fixture.
    runner = object.__new__(GatewayRunner)
    runner.config = GatewayConfig(multiplex_profiles=True)
    runner._served_profile_homes = workspace.runner._served_profile_homes
    runner.adapters = {Platform.SLACK: workspace.adapter}
    runner._running_agents = {}
    runner._pending_messages = {}
    runner._delivery_adapter_for = lambda source: workspace.adapter
    runner._owning_profile = lambda adapter, platform: (True, 'default')
    runner._persist_active_agents = lambda: None
    workspace.adapter.gateway_runner = runner
    workspace.runner = runner
    monkeypatch.setattr('hermes_cli.plugins.invoke_hook', lambda *args, **kwargs: None)
    return runner


async def running(workspace, event):
    runner = workspace.runner
    key = runner._session_key_for_source(event.source)
    reasons = []
    runner._running_agents[key] = SimpleNamespace(session_id=key, hard_interrupt=reasons.append)
    task = asyncio.create_task(asyncio.Event().wait())
    workspace.adapter._session_tasks[key] = task
    workspace.adapter._active_sessions[key] = asyncio.Event()
    return key, reasons, task


class CleanupBrowser:
    def __init__(self):
        self.homes = []
        self.fail = None

    def stop(self, turn, session=None, *, purge=False):
        self.homes.append((turn.home, purge, turn.source.user_id))
        if turn.home == self.fail:
            raise AccessError('Fixture cleanup unavailable', 409)

async def test_configured_cloud_control_does_not_reauthorize_cancelled_worker(workspace, monkeypatch, control_source):

def native_runner(workspace, monkeypatch):
    # Retain the real key derivation, run generations, hard interruption and
    # native release path; only platform/plugin I/O is a fixture.
    runner = object.__new__(GatewayRunner)
    runner.config = GatewayConfig(multiplex_profiles=True)
    runner._served_profile_homes = workspace.runner._served_profile_homes
    runner.adapters = {Platform.SLACK: workspace.adapter}
    runner._running_agents = {}
    runner._pending_messages = {}
    runner._delivery_adapter_for = lambda source: workspace.adapter
    runner._owning_profile = lambda adapter, platform: (True, 'default')
    runner._persist_active_agents = lambda: None
    workspace.adapter.gateway_runner = runner
    workspace.runner = runner
    monkeypatch.setattr('hermes_cli.plugins.invoke_hook', lambda *args, **kwargs: None)
    return runner


async def running(workspace, event):
    runner = workspace.runner
    key = runner._session_key_for_source(event.source)
    reasons = []
    runner._running_agents[key] = SimpleNamespace(session_id=key, hard_interrupt=reasons.append)
    task = asyncio.create_task(asyncio.Event().wait())
    workspace.adapter._session_tasks[key] = task
    workspace.adapter._active_sessions[key] = asyncio.Event()
    return key, reasons, task


class CleanupBrowser:
    def __init__(self):
        self.homes = []
        self.fail = None

    def stop(self, turn, session=None, *, purge=False):
        self.homes.append((turn.home, purge, turn.source.user_id))
        if turn.home == self.fail:
            raise AccessError('Fixture cleanup unavailable', 409)

def native_runner(workspace, monkeypatch):
    # Retain the real key derivation, run generations, hard interruption and
    # native release path; only platform/plugin I/O is a fixture.
    runner = object.__new__(GatewayRunner)
    runner.config = GatewayConfig(multiplex_profiles=True)
    runner._served_profile_homes = workspace.runner._served_profile_homes
    runner.adapters = {Platform.SLACK: workspace.adapter}
    runner._running_agents = {}
    runner._pending_messages = {}
    runner._delivery_adapter_for = lambda source: workspace.adapter
    runner._owning_profile = lambda adapter, platform: (True, 'default')
    runner._persist_active_agents = lambda: None
    workspace.adapter.gateway_runner = runner
    workspace.runner = runner
    monkeypatch.setattr('hermes_cli.plugins.invoke_hook', lambda *args, **kwargs: None)
    return runner


async def running(workspace, event):
    runner = workspace.runner
    key = runner._session_key_for_source(event.source)
    reasons = []
    runner._running_agents[key] = SimpleNamespace(session_id=key, hard_interrupt=reasons.append)
    task = asyncio.create_task(asyncio.Event().wait())
    workspace.adapter._session_tasks[key] = task
    workspace.adapter._active_sessions[key] = asyncio.Event()
    return key, reasons, task


class CleanupBrowser:
    def __init__(self):
        self.homes = []
        self.fail = None

    def stop(self, turn, session=None, *, purge=False):
        self.homes.append((turn.home, purge, turn.source.user_id))
        if turn.home == self.fail:
            raise AccessError('Fixture cleanup unavailable', 409)

@pytest.mark.parametrize('failure_stage', ['cloud', 'interrupt'])
async def test_revocation_migrates_usage_and_cleans_every_used_task_home(workspace, monkeypatch, failure_stage):
    await provision(workspace)
    _, first = await detour(workspace, owner='UB', task='Read the first invited dashboard.')
    _, second = await detour(workspace, owner='UB', thread='200.2', task='Read the second invited dashboard.')
    runner = native_runner(workspace, monkeypatch)
    first_key, first_reasons, first_task = await running(workspace, first)
    _, second_reasons, second_task = await running(workspace, second)
    service = workspace.service
    meta = VaultStore(service.private_home('TT', 'UA') / 'vault').add_item('login', 'Dummy invited login',
        {'identifier': 'dummy@example.invalid', 'identifier_type': 'email', 'password': 'REDACTED'},
        origin='https://accounts.example.com')
    grant = service.delegations.invite({'team': 'TT', 'owner': 'UA'}, meta.id, 'UB')['id']
    actors = [worker_turn(workspace, event) for event in (first, second)]
    # Exercise the actual old schema migration with a retained first-home marker.
    with service.store.connection() as db:
        db.executescript('''DROP TABLE credential_grant_usage;
            CREATE TABLE credential_grant_usage (grant_id TEXT NOT NULL, team TEXT NOT NULL,
              recipient TEXT NOT NULL, home TEXT NOT NULL, source TEXT NOT NULL,
              PRIMARY KEY(grant_id,team,recipient));''')
        db.execute('INSERT INTO credential_grant_usage VALUES (?,?,?,?,?)',
            (grant, 'TT', 'UB', str(actors[0].home), json.dumps(first.source.to_dict())))
    service.delegations = Delegations(service)
    for actor in actors:
        service.delegations.record_browser_use(actor, service.delegations.resolve(actor, grant))
    with service.store.connection() as db:
        assert db.execute('SELECT count(*) FROM credential_grant_usage').fetchone()[0] == 2
    browser = CleanupBrowser()
    real_interrupt = runner._interrupt_and_clear_session
    if failure_stage == 'cloud':
        browser.fail = actors[0].home
    else:
        async def failing_interrupt(key, *args, **kwargs):
            if key == first_key:
                raise AccessError('Fixture native interruption unavailable', 503)
            return await real_interrupt(key, *args, **kwargs)
        runner._interrupt_and_clear_session = failing_interrupt
    service.cloud_browser = browser
    try:
        result = await service.revoke_invitation({'team': 'TT', 'owner': 'UA'}, grant)
        assert result == {'revoked': True, 'cleanup_pending': True}
        assert second_reasons and first_task.cancelled() and second_task.cancelled()
        assert bool(first_reasons) == (failure_stage == 'cloud')
        assert {home for home, purge, _ in browser.homes if purge} == {actor.home for actor in actors}
        with service.store.connection() as db:
            rows = db.execute('SELECT home FROM credential_grant_usage').fetchall()
        assert [row[0] for row in rows] == [str(actors[0].home)]
        with pytest.raises(AccessError):
            service.delegations.check_execution(actors[1])
        browser.fail = None
        runner._interrupt_and_clear_session = real_interrupt
        assert await service.revoke_invitation({'team': 'TT', 'owner': 'UA'}, grant) == {
            'revoked': True, 'cleanup_pending': False}
        with service.store.connection() as db:
            assert db.execute('SELECT count(*) FROM credential_grant_usage').fetchone()[0] == 0
        assert VaultStore(service.private_home('TT', 'UA') / 'vault').get_meta(meta.id)
    finally:
        for task in (first_task, second_task):
            task.cancel()
        await asyncio.gather(first_task, second_task, return_exceptions=True)

import threading
from types import SimpleNamespace
from unittest.mock import MagicMock

from agent.gateway_context import IsolatedGatewayTask, current_gateway_turn, gateway_turn_scope
from gateway.config import Platform
from gateway.platforms.event import MessageEvent
from gateway.run import GatewayRunner
from gateway.run_turn_runner import TurnRunner
from gateway.session import SessionSource
from gateway.turn_context import TurnContext


def test_native_turn_binds_conversation_for_task_handoff_without_mutating_history(tmp_path, monkeypatch):
    monkeypatch.setenv('HERMES_HOME', str(tmp_path))
    source = SessionSource(Platform.SLACK, 'C1', user_id='U1', scope_id='T1', thread_id='100.1')
    history = [{'role': 'user', 'content': 'Find the earliest Mumbai flight on 9 October.'},
               {'role': 'assistant', 'content': [{'type': 'text', 'text': 'Where from?'}]},
               {'role': 'tool', 'content': 'PRIVATE_TOOL_CANARY'}]
    before = repr(history)
    captured = []

    class Agent:
        def run_conversation(self, message, **kwargs):
            captured.append(current_gateway_turn())
            assert kwargs['conversation_history'] is history
            return {'final_response': 'continued'}

    runner = SimpleNamespace(_consume_pending_native_image_paths=lambda key: [])
    ctx = TurnContext(source=source, session_id='flight-session', session_key='flight-lane',
                      message='NGP', inbound_message_id='100.2')
    result = TurnRunner(runner, ctx)._run_conversation_with_approval(Agent(), history, '', None, None)
    assert result['final_response'] == 'continued'
    assert captured[0].conversation == (
        ('user', history[0]['content']), ('assistant', 'Where from?'))
    assert captured[0].message == 'NGP' and captured[0].message_id == '100.2'
    assert repr(history) == before and current_gateway_turn() is None


def test_worker_capability_is_not_wire_data_and_owns_full_reply(monkeypatch, tmp_path):
    monkeypatch.setenv("HERMES_HOME", str(tmp_path))
    captured = []

    async def respond(event, response, runner):
        captured.append((event, response, runner))

    source = SessionSource(Platform.SLACK, "D1", user_id="U1", scope_id="T1")
    source.isolated_task = IsolatedGatewayTask("task-1", respond)
    restored = SessionSource.from_dict({**source.to_dict(), "isolated_task": source.isolated_task})
    assert restored.isolated_task is None
    assert "isolated_task" not in source.to_dict()
    assert "respond" not in repr(source)
    with gateway_turn_scope("runner", source, "session-1", "request", message_id="resume-1"):
        assert current_gateway_turn().message_id == "resume-1"
    assert current_gateway_turn() is None

    runner = object.__new__(GatewayRunner)
    runner._delivery_adapter_for = MagicMock(side_effect=AssertionError("ordinary egress entered"))
    event = MessageEvent("continue", source=source)
    response = "complete result " * 100
    result = asyncio.run(runner._hmwa_deliver_turn_response(
        event, source, None, "worker", None, {"already_sent": True}, [], response, "footer", False,
    ))
    assert result is None
    assert captured == [(event, response, runner)]
    runner._delivery_adapter_for.assert_not_called()

    async def failed_publication(*_args):
        raise RuntimeError("publication unavailable")

    source.isolated_task = IsolatedGatewayTask("task-1", failed_publication)
    assert asyncio.run(runner._hmwa_deliver_turn_response(
        event, source, None, "worker", None, {}, [], response, None, False,
    )) is None
    runner._delivery_adapter_for.assert_not_called()

        full thread + root images once, set watermark. Session + @mention: delta past watermark
        (cache bypassed). Session, first plain reply this process: restart rehydration; later
        replies only advance the watermark. Context goes into the NEW turn only (prompt caching)."""

        #   ``channel_context``) — prior conversation history is never rewritten, so prompt caching is

        #   conversational text. ``channel_context`` is prepended only after command dispatch.

Per-file parallel test runner.

The minimum-viable replacement for pytest-xdist + a subprocess-isolation
plugin. Discovers test files under ``tests/`` (excluding integration/e2e
unless explicitly requested), then runs one ``python -m pytest <file>``
subprocess per file, with bounded parallelism (default: ``os.cpu_count()``).

Why per-file rather than per-test?
    Per-test spawn overhead (~250ms × 17k tests = 70min CPU minimum)
    swamped the actual work. Per-file spawn (~250ms × ~850 files = ~3.5min)
    fits in the budget while still giving every file a fresh Python
    interpreter — the only isolation boundary that actually matters
    (cross-file module-level state leakage was the original flake source;
    intra-file state is the test author's responsibility).

Why drop xdist entirely?
    xdist's persistent workers accumulate state across files, which is
    exactly the leakage we wanted to fix. xdist also adds complexity
    (loadfile vs loadscope, --max-worker-restart, internal control plane)
    that we don't need when the unit of work is "run pytest on one file".
    A subprocess.Popen pool gated by a semaphore is ~60 lines and does
    the job.

Usage:
    python scripts/run_tests_parallel.py [pytest_args...]

    Common pytest args pass through to each per-file pytest invocation
    (e.g. ``-q``, ``-v``, ``-x``, ``--tb=long``, ``-k 'pattern'``, ``--lf``)
    with no special separator — a bare ``-q`` "just works". Anything after
    a literal ``--`` is also passed through, and stacks with bare flags.
    ``-h``/``--help`` prints this usage; a bare flag pytest does not know
    (a typo like ``--jbs``) is a usage error here rather than a per-file
    pytest failure. Tokens after ``--`` are never validated.

positional arguments:

  --paths PATHS         Colon-separated discovery roots (default: 'tests'). On

try:
    async def _hydrate_thread_context(
        self, *, channel_id: str, event_thread_ts, ts: str, user_id: str, team_id: str,
        is_thread_reply: bool, is_mentioned: bool, is_dm: bool,
    ) -> Tuple[Optional[str], List[str], List[str]]:
        """``(channel_context, root_media_urls, root_media_types)`` for a thread reply. No session:
        full thread + root images once, set watermark. Session + @mention: delta past watermark
        (cache bypassed). Session, first plain reply this process: restart rehydration; later
        replies only advance the watermark. Context goes into the NEW turn only (prompt caching)."""
        # - Active thread + explicit @mention: refresh with only the delta since the last hydrate/refresh
        #   (#23918), bypassing the TTL cache. The delta is injected as part of the NEW turn (via
        #   ``channel_context``) — prior conversation history is never rewritten, so prompt caching is
        #   preserved. Keep recovered history separate from ``text``. Prepending it here moves a recognized
        #   command away from character zero, so downstream command routing can misclassify it as
        #   conversational text. ``channel_context`` is prepended only after command dispatch.
        channel_context = None
        # Thread-root images recovered on the cold-start hydrate: when the bot is mentioned mid-thread for
        # the first time, the thread root is very often the artifact the mention is about ("@bot what's in
        # this chart?" replying under an image post) — deliver its images with this first turn. One-time by
        # construction: the cold-start path is guarded by _has_active_session_for_thread, so subsequent
        # turns in the same session never re-deliver (adapted from #69185).
        thread_root_media_urls: List[str] = []
        thread_root_media_types: List[str] = []
        if not is_thread_reply:
            return channel_context, thread_root_media_urls, thread_root_media_types
        has_active_thread_session = self._has_active_session_for_thread(
            channel_id=channel_id, thread_ts=event_thread_ts, user_id=user_id, team_id=team_id,
            chat_type="dm" if is_dm else "group")

        async def _fetch(**kw) -> None:
            nonlocal channel_context
            thread_context = await self._fetch_thread_context(
                channel_id=channel_id, thread_ts=event_thread_ts, current_ts=ts, team_id=team_id,
                **kw)
            if thread_context:
                channel_context = thread_context

        watermark_args = dict(
            channel_id=channel_id, thread_ts=event_thread_ts, user_id=user_id, team_id=team_id)
        if not has_active_thread_session:
            await _fetch()
            (
                thread_root_media_urls, thread_root_media_types,
            ) = await self._collect_thread_root_images(
                channel_id=channel_id, thread_ts=event_thread_ts, team_id=team_id)
        elif is_mentioned:
            await _fetch(after_ts=self._get_thread_watermark(**watermark_args), force_refresh=True)
        else:
            # Restart rehydration (#63530 restart gap / #33215): persistent sessions survive gateway
            # restarts, but thread replies posted while the gateway was down never reached the session. On
            # the FIRST ordinary reply per thread in this process, fetch the delta past the persisted
            # watermark and inject anything missed as part of this new turn. Checked at most once per thread
            # per process; a non-empty watermark plus an empty delta costs one cached conversations.replies
            # call.
            rehydration_key = self._thread_rehydration_key(
                channel_id, event_thread_ts, user_id, team_id)
            if rehydration_key in self._thread_rehydration_checked:
                self._set_thread_watermark(watermark_ts=ts, **watermark_args)
                return channel_context, thread_root_media_urls, thread_root_media_types
            watermark_ts = self._get_thread_watermark(**watermark_args)
            if watermark_ts:
                await _fetch(after_ts=watermark_ts, force_refresh=True)
        self._set_thread_watermark(watermark_ts=ts, **watermark_args)
        self._mark_thread_rehydration_checked(channel_id, event_thread_ts, user_id, team_id)
        return channel_context, thread_root_media_urls, thread_root_media_types

        # construction: the cold-start path is guarded by _has_active_session_for_thread, so subsequent

        thread_root_media_types: List[str] = []

            channel_id=channel_id, thread_ts=event_thread_ts, user_id=user_id, team_id=team_id,

                channel_id=channel_id, thread_ts=event_thread_ts, current_ts=ts, team_id=team_id,
                **kw)
            if thread_context:

        watermark_args = dict(
            channel_id=channel_id, thread_ts=event_thread_ts, user_id=user_id, team_id=team_id)
        if not has_active_thread_session:
            await _fetch()

                thread_root_media_urls, thread_root_media_types,
            ) = await self._collect_thread_root_images(
                channel_id=channel_id, thread_ts=event_thread_ts, team_id=team_id)
        elif is_mentioned:
            await _fetch(after_ts=self._get_thread_watermark(**watermark_args), force_refresh=True)
        else:

            # restarts, but thread replies posted while the gateway was down never reached the session. On
            # the FIRST ordinary reply per thread in this process, fetch the delta past the persisted
            # watermark and inject anything missed as part of this new turn. Checked at most once per thread
            # per process; a non-empty watermark plus an empty delta costs one cached conversations.replies
            # call.
            rehydration_key = self._thread_rehydration_key(
                channel_id, event_thread_ts, user_id, team_id)
            if rehydration_key in self._thread_rehydration_checked:
                self._set_thread_watermark(watermark_ts=ts, **watermark_args)
                return channel_context, thread_root_media_urls, thread_root_media_types
            watermark_ts = self._get_thread_watermark(**watermark_args)
            if watermark_ts:
                await _fetch(after_ts=watermark_ts, force_refresh=True)
        self._set_thread_watermark(watermark_ts=ts, **watermark_args)
        self._mark_thread_rehydration_checked(channel_id, event_thread_ts, user_id, team_id)
        return channel_context, thread_root_media_urls, thread_root_media_types

Per-file parallel test runner.

The minimum-viable replacement for pytest-xdist + a subprocess-isolation
plugin. Discovers test files under ``tests/`` (excluding integration/e2e
unless explicitly requested), then runs one ``python -m pytest <file>``
subprocess per file, with bounded parallelism (default: ``os.cpu_count()``).

Why per-file rather than per-test?
    Per-test spawn overhead (~250ms × 17k tests = 70min CPU minimum)
    swamped the actual work. Per-file spawn (~250ms × ~850 files = ~3.5min)
    fits in the budget while still giving every file a fresh Python
    interpreter — the only isolation boundary that actually matters
    (cross-file module-level state leakage was the original flake source;
    intra-file state is the test author's responsibility).

Why drop xdist entirely?
    xdist's persistent workers accumulate state across files, which is
    exactly the leakage we wanted to fix. xdist also adds complexity
    (loadfile vs loadscope, --max-worker-restart, internal control plane)
    that we don't need when the unit of work is "run pytest on one file".
    A subprocess.Popen pool gated by a semaphore is ~60 lines and does
    the job.

Usage:
    python scripts/run_tests_parallel.py [pytest_args...]

    (e.g. ``-q``, ``-v``, ``-x``, ``--tb=long``, ``-k 'pattern'``, ``--lf``)
    with no special separator — a bare ``-q`` "just works". Anything after
    a literal ``--`` is also passed through, and stacks with bare flags.
    ``-h``/``--help`` prints this usage; a bare flag pytest does not know
    (a typo like ``--jbs``) is a usage error here rather than a per-file
    pytest failure. Tokens after ``--`` are never validated.

    await adapter._handle_slack_message(edit("edited during intake", "111.001", "110.001"))
    release_enrichment.set()
    await asyncio.wait_for(intake, 5)

"""Real Slack intake and durable task routing; transport and model are fixtures."""
import asyncio
import json
from types import SimpleNamespace
from unittest.mock import AsyncMock

import pytest

from test_clanker_channel_tasks import workspace, provision, channel_turn, settle, worker_turn
from agent.gateway_context import isolated_gateway_task
from agent.vault_store import VaultStore
from gateway.config import Platform, PlatformConfig
from gateway.run import GatewayRunner
from gateway.session import build_session_key
from plugins.platforms.slack.adapter import SlackAdapter
from vault.service import VaultService


def native_intake(workspace):
    adapter = SlackAdapter(PlatformConfig(enabled=True, token='xoxb-fixture',
        typing_indicator=False, extra={'reactions': False}))
    runner = object.__new__(GatewayRunner)
    runner.config = SimpleNamespace(multiplex_profiles=True, profile_routes=[])
    runner._served_profile_homes = workspace.runner._served_profile_homes
    runner.adapters = {Platform.SLACK: adapter}
    adapter.gateway_runner = runner
    adapter._team_clients = {'TT': workspace.client}
    adapter._team_bot_user_ids = {'TT': 'UBOT'}
    adapter._bot_user_id = 'UBOT'
    adapter._workspace_membership = workspace.policy
    adapter._resolve_user_name = AsyncMock(return_value='Fixture member')
    adapter._resolve_channel_name = AsyncMock(return_value='Fixture conversation')
    adapter._hydrate_thread_context = AsyncMock(return_value=(None, [], []))
    adapter._set_assistant_thread_title = AsyncMock()
    captured = []
    async def dispatch(a, event, revision, **kwargs):
        a._canonicalize(event.source)
        assert workspace.policy.authorize_source(event.source)
        captured.append(event)
    adapter._message_edits.dispatch = dispatch
    workspace.policy.adapter = adapter
    return adapter, captured


async def intake(workspace, adapter, owner, chat, thread, ts, text):
    workspace.client.conversations_info.return_value = {'channel':
        {'is_im': True, 'user': owner} if chat.startswith('D') else {'is_member': True}}
    await adapter._handle_slack_message({'type': 'message', 'user': owner,
        'channel': chat, 'channel_type': 'im' if chat.startswith('D') else 'channel',
        'team': 'TT', 'ts': ts, 'thread_ts': thread, 'text': text,
        'client_msg_id': 'human-' + ts})


@pytest.mark.asyncio
async def test_native_dm_replies_keep_flight_worker_after_restart_and_deliver_each_turn(workspace):
    await provision(workspace)
    selected = 'Nagpur to Mumbai on 9 October, one adult, AI-2584 at 10:10 PM, accepted INR 6540.'
    events = []
    for index, owner in enumerate(('UA', 'UB', 'UA')):
        turn = channel_turn(workspace, owner=owner, task='yeah', thread='200.' + str(index),
                            message_id='300.' + str(index))
        turn.conversation = (('user', selected), ('assistant', 'Continue the selected booking privately.'))
        await workspace.service.move_private(turn)
        await settle(workspace.service)
        initial = workspace.events[-1]
        await workspace.service.channel_tasks.handle_response(initial, 'Signed in; passenger details are still needed.', workspace.runner)
        events.append(initial)
    restored = VaultService(workspace.policy, workspace.service.config)
    workspace.policy.vault_service = restored
    workspace.service = restored
    adapter, captured = native_intake(workspace)
    for index, initial in enumerate(events):
        owner = initial.source.user_id
        before = len(captured)
        await intake(workspace, adapter, owner, initial.source.chat_id, initial.source.thread_id,
                     '400.' + str(index), 'go further now')
        assert len(captured) == before + 1
        reply = captured[-1]
        assert reply.source.profile == initial.source.profile
        assert isolated_gateway_task(reply.source).task_id == isolated_gateway_task(initial.source).task_id
        assert build_session_key(reply.source, profile=reply.source.profile) == build_session_key(initial.source, profile=initial.source.profile)
        assert selected in reply.channel_context and 'go further now' == reply.text
        result = 'The selected flight is ready for passenger details, task ' + str(index)
        await restored.channel_tasks.handle_response(reply, result, adapter.gateway_runner)
        posted = [m for m in workspace.messages if m['channel'] == 'CSHARED' and m.get('thread_ts') == '200.' + str(index)]
        assert [m['text'] for m in posted] == ['Signed in; passenger details are still needed.', result]
        assert len({m['client_msg_id'] for m in posted}) == 2
        # A duplicate intake after another restart cannot reopen a delivered turn.
        restored = VaultService(workspace.policy, restored.config)
        workspace.policy.vault_service = restored
        workspace.service = restored
        adapter._processed_message_ts.clear()
        await intake(workspace, adapter, owner, initial.source.chat_id, initial.source.thread_id,
                     '400.' + str(index), 'go further now')
        assert len(captured) == before + 1
    # Another owner cannot adopt the private worker by quoting its DM thread.
    await intake(workspace, adapter, 'UB', 'DUB', events[0].source.thread_id, '500.1', 'continue')
    assert captured[-1].source.profile == workspace.policy.state['members']['UB']['profile']
    assert isolated_gateway_task(captured[-1].source) is None


@pytest.mark.asyncio
async def test_code_waiting_reply_and_public_status_share_one_task_without_false_delivery(workspace):
    await provision(workspace)
    turn = channel_turn(workspace, task='Continue selected AI-2584 flight', message_id='200.2')
    await workspace.service.move_private(turn)
    await settle(workspace.service)
    initial = workspace.events[-1]
    owner_home = workspace.service.private_home('TT', 'UA')
    meta = VaultStore(owner_home / 'vault').add_item('login', 'Fixture flights',
        {'identifier': 'fixture@example.invalid', 'identifier_type': 'email', 'password': 'REDACTED'},
        origin='https://flights.invalid')
    form = await workspace.service.request_code(worker_turn(workspace, initial), meta)
    adapter, captured = native_intake(workspace)
    await intake(workspace, adapter, 'UA', 'DUA', initial.source.thread_id, '600.1', 'we good now?')
    reply = captured[-1]
    assert reply.source.profile == initial.source.profile
    await workspace.service.channel_tasks.handle_response(reply, 'Your verification form is still waiting.', adapter.gateway_runner)
    assert workspace.messages[-1]['channel'] == 'DUA'
    assert workspace.messages[-1]['thread_ts'] == initial.source.thread_id
    assert workspace.service.store.channel_task(reply.source.to_dict())['task_state'] == 'active'
    assert not any(m['channel'] == 'CSHARED' for m in workspace.messages)
    await intake(workspace, adapter, 'UA', 'CSHARED', '200.1', '600.2', '<@UBOT> sent the code')
    public = captured[-1]
    assert isolated_gateway_task(public.source) is None
    assert 'verification form: waiting' in public.channel_context
    workspace.client.conversations_info.return_value = {'channel': {'is_member': True}}
    await workspace.service.move_private(channel_turn(workspace, task='sent the code', message_id='600.2'))
    await settle(workspace.service)
    with workspace.service.store.connection() as db:
        assert db.execute('SELECT count(*) FROM transfers').fetchone()[0] == 1
    workspace.service.save_code(form['request_id'], workspace.service.store.token(form['request_id']),
                               {'team': 'TT', 'owner': 'UA'}, {'code': '731924'})
    # Submitted is a backend fact, never a claim that the merchant accepted it.
    await intake(workspace, adapter, 'UA', 'CSHARED', '200.1', '600.3', '<@UBOT> code submitted')
    assert 'verification form: submitted' in captured[-1].channel_context
    assert '731924' not in captured[-1].channel_context

        source = event.source
        revision = getattr(event,'_slack_revision',None)
        if revision and not self.service.policy.adapter._message_edits.current(revision):
            return
        row = self.store.channel_task(source.to_dict())
        if row is None or row['task_state'] in ('cancelled','completed'):
            return
        if row['task_state']=='active':
            self.execution_route(source)
            # The trusted handler already sent the form to the owner's DM.
            # A waiting model reply is not the channel task's final answer.
            waiting = self.store.channel_task_waiting(source.to_dict())
            human_reply = source.message_id==event.message_id
            if (self.store.channel_task_requested_access(source.to_dict(),event.message_id) or
                    waiting and not human_reply):
                return
            if not response.strip():
                raise AccessError('The account task did not produce a result.',409)
            # Capture before optional vault reads and Slack I/O. A failed
            # redaction or publication must retry the answer, never the work.
            event_key = self.event_key(event)
            queued_reply = bool(row['last_inbound_id'] and row['last_inbound_id']!=event_key)
            self.store.save_channel_result(row['id'],response,event_id=event_key,
                                           private=waiting and human_reply,continuing=waiting or queued_reply)
        await self.deliver(row['id'])

    async def deliver(self, task_id):
        lock = self.delivery_locks.setdefault(task_id,asyncio.Lock())
        async with lock:
            row = next((item for item in self.store.pending_channel_results() if item['id']==task_id),None)
            if row is None:
                return
            original = await self.validate_destination(row)
            target = json.loads(row['source']) if row['result_private'] else original.to_dict()
            edits = getattr(self.service.policy.adapter, '_message_edits', None)
            revision = edits.lookup((original.scope_id, original.chat_id, original.user_id,
                                     original.message_id)) if edits and original.message_id else None
            request_version = json.loads(row['original_source']).get('slack_request_version')
            request_digest = json.loads(row['original_source']).get('slack_request_digest')
            if (revision and request_version and str(revision.version) != request_version
                    and revision.digest != request_digest):
                return  # an edit was admitted while this result was waiting for publication
            client = self.service.policy.client()
            client_id = str(uuid5(NAMESPACE_URL,'clanker-channel-result:' + task_id +
                                 (':' + row['result_event_id'] if row['result_event_id'] else '')))
            # Recover a Slack ACK lost before the SQLite completion commit.
            cursor = None
            posted = None
            while True:
                args = {'channel':target['chat_id'],'ts':target['thread_id'],'limit':100}
                if cursor:args['cursor']=cursor
                history = await client.conversations_replies(**args)
                posted = next((m for m in history.get('messages',[]) if m.get('client_msg_id')==client_id),None)
                cursor = history.get('response_metadata',{}).get('next_cursor')
                if posted or not cursor:break
            if posted is None:
                # Cancellation may have happened while waiting for Slack.
                row = next((item for item in self.store.pending_channel_results() if item['id']==task_id),None)
                if row is None:return
                await self.validate_destination(row)
                # Membership refresh awaits Slack. Honor a cancellation that
                # committed during that refresh before beginning publication.
                row = next((item for item in self.store.pending_channel_results() if item['id']==task_id),None)
                if row is None:return
                text = self.store.code_crypto().decrypt(row['result_payload']).decode()
                from agent.vault_store import scrub_secret_from_text
                from agent.redact import redact_registered_vault_values, redact_sensitive_text
                from gateway.run import _profile_runtime_scope
                # Outbox recovery runs outside the turn. Rebuild this owner's
                # contact scrubbing under the worker scope before publication.
                with _profile_runtime_scope(self.home(row)):
                    self.service.personal.register_redactions(SimpleNamespace(source=original))
                    for item in self.service.delegations.items(row['team'],row['owner']):
                        access = self.service.delegations.lookup(row['team'],row['owner'],item['id'])
                        text = scrub_secret_from_text(text,access.secret())
                    text = redact_registered_vault_values(redact_sensitive_text(text,force=True))
                if revision and not edits.current(revision):
                    return
                if revision and revision.reply.ids and row['result_message_ts'] is None and not row['result_private']:
                    result = await edits.update_reply(self.service.policy.adapter, revision, text,
                        {'slack_team_id':original.scope_id,'thread_id':original.thread_id})
                    if not result.success:
                        raise AccessError('The updated channel result remains pending.', 409)
                    posted = {'ts':result.message_id}
                else:
                    posted = await client.chat_postMessage(channel=target['chat_id'],thread_ts=target['thread_id'],
                        text=text,client_msg_id=client_id,unfurl_links=False,unfurl_media=False)
                    if revision and row['result_message_ts'] is None and not row['result_private']:
                        revision.reply.ids.append(posted['ts'])
                        await edits.save(revision)
            self.store.mark_channel_result(task_id,posted['ts'])

    def recover_response(self, row, event_id):
        """Adopt a completed native reply after a coordinator-store crash gap."""
        from hermes_state import SessionDB
        database = SessionDB(db_path=self.home(row)/'state.db')
        try:
            anchor = database._read_one("SELECT id,session_id FROM messages WHERE role='user' "
                "AND platform_message_id=? ORDER BY id DESC LIMIT 1",(event_id,))
            if anchor is None:return None
            tail = database.get_messages(anchor['session_id'],after_id=anchor['id'])
            if not tail or any(message['role']=='user' for message in tail):return None
            final = tail[-1]
            if final['role']=='assistant' and not final.get('tool_calls') and isinstance(final.get('content'),str):
                return final['content']
            return None
        finally:
            database.close()

    async def drain(self):
        for row in self.store.pending_channel_results():
            try:
                await self.deliver(row['id'])
            except Exception:
                # The encrypted outbox retains the exact response for the next pass.
                continue

@pytest.mark.asyncio
async def test_code_waiting_reply_and_public_status_share_one_task_without_false_delivery(workspace):
    await provision(workspace)
    workspace.client.chat_getPermalink = AsyncMock(side_effect=lambda channel,message_ts:
        {'permalink':'https://slack.invalid/archives/' + channel + '/p' + message_ts.replace('.','')})
    turn = channel_turn(workspace, task='Continue selected AI-2584 flight', message_id='200.2')
    moved = await workspace.service.move_private(turn)
    assert moved['private_thread_url'].startswith('https://slack.invalid/archives/DUA/')
    await settle(workspace.service)
    initial = workspace.events[-1]
    owner_home = workspace.service.private_home('TT', 'UA')
    meta = VaultStore(owner_home / 'vault').add_item('login', 'Fixture flights',
        {'identifier': 'fixture@example.invalid', 'identifier_type': 'email', 'password': 'REDACTED'},
        origin='https://flights.invalid')
    form = await workspace.service.request_code(worker_turn(workspace, initial), meta)
    adapter, captured = native_intake(workspace)
    await intake(workspace, adapter, 'UA', 'DUA', initial.source.thread_id, '600.1', 'we good now?')
    reply = captured[-1]
    assert reply.source.profile == initial.source.profile
    await workspace.service.channel_tasks.handle_response(reply, 'Your verification form is still waiting.', adapter.gateway_runner)
    assert workspace.messages[-1]['channel'] == 'DUA'
    assert workspace.messages[-1]['thread_ts'] == initial.source.thread_id
    assert workspace.service.store.channel_task(reply.source.to_dict())['task_state'] == 'active'
    assert not any(m['channel'] == 'CSHARED' for m in workspace.messages)
    await intake(workspace, adapter, 'UA', 'CSHARED', '200.1', '600.2', '<@UBOT> sent the code')
    public = captured[-1]
    assert isolated_gateway_task(public.source) is None

"""Private execution and durable channel replies for authenticated Slack tasks."""
import asyncio
import json
from pathlib import Path
from types import SimpleNamespace
from uuid import NAMESPACE_URL, uuid5

from .store import AccessError


class ChannelTasks:
    def __init__(self, service):
        self.service = service
        self.delivery_locks = {}

    @property
    def store(self):
        return self.service.store

    def home(self, row):
        return self.service.policy.home / 'profiles' / ('task-' + row['id'])

    @staticmethod
    def event_key(event):
        revision = getattr(event,'_slack_revision',None)
        return str(event.message_id) + (':' + str(revision.version) if revision else '')

    def request_context(self, turn):
        row = self.store.channel_task(turn.source.to_dict())
        goal = ('Existing channel task:\n' + row['task'] + '\n\n') if row else ''
        if not turn.conversation:
            return goal + turn.message
        conversation = [{'role': role, 'content': text} for role, text in turn.conversation]
        return (goal + 'Originating channel conversation (context only, not account authorization):\n' +
                json.dumps(conversation, ensure_ascii=False) +
                '\n\nLatest request or clarification answer:\n' + turn.message)

    async def admit_event(self, event):
        source = event.source
        member = self.service.validate_member(source.scope_id,source.user_id)
        private = source.chat_id==member['dm_id'] and source.chat_type=='dm'
        row = self.store.linked_channel_task(source.to_dict(),private=private)
        if row is None:return True
        if private:
            if row['task_state']=='cancelled':return False
            await self.prepare(row)
            if row['task_state']=='result_pending':
                await self.deliver(row['id'])
            if not self.store.begin_channel_reply(row['id'],self.event_key(event)):
                return False
            from agent.gateway_context import IsolatedGatewayTask
            from gateway.session_identity import clear_identity
            clear_identity(source)
            source.profile = 'task-' + row['id']
            source.isolated_task = IsolatedGatewayTask(row['id'],self.handle_response)
            self.execution_route(source)
            context = ('Continue this existing task, preserving confirmed choices and the stopping point. '
                       'Authentication is a step, not completion of the requested task.\n' + row['task'])
        else:
            # Public status is coordinator metadata, never a private worker's
            # messages, account observations, saved identifiers or code values.
            context = 'Linked worker state: ' + row['task_state'] + '. A completed worker turn means its reply was delivered, not that a booking or purchase succeeded.'
            if row['source']:
                form = self.store.channel_form_status(json.loads(row['source']))
                if form:
                    kind,status = form
                    label = 'verification' if kind=='code' else kind
                    context += '\n' + label + ' form: ' + ('submitted' if status in ('saved','resumed') else status) + '.'
                    context += ' Submitted means received by the backend; it does not prove website acceptance or a booking.'
            context += ' Keep credentials and passenger/contact details in the linked private DM. Do not start another handoff for a status check.'
        event.channel_context = '\n\n'.join(part for part in (event.channel_context,context) if part)
        return True

    def execution_route(self, source):
        from agent.gateway_context import isolated_gateway_task
        task = isolated_gateway_task(source)
        row = self.store.channel_task(source.to_dict())
        if (task is None or row is None or task.task_id!=row['id'] or
                row['task_state']!='active' or source.chat_id!=self.service.validate_member(
                    row['team'],row['owner'])['dm_id']):
            raise AccessError('This isolated account task is no longer authorized.',403)
        original = json.loads(row['original_source'])
        policy = self.service.policy
        if (not policy.authorize_sender(row['owner'],original['chat_id']) or
                self.service.private_home(row['team'],row['owner'])!=Path(row['home'])):
            raise AccessError('The original account task is no longer authorized.',403)
        return 'task-' + row['id']

    def restore(self, source):
        """Restore a coordinator resume; native owner replies use admit_event."""
        from agent.gateway_context import IsolatedGatewayTask
        row = self.store.channel_task(source.to_dict())
        if row is None:
            return None
        source.isolated_task = IsolatedGatewayTask(row['id'], self.handle_response)
        return row

    async def validate_destination(self, row):
        from gateway.session import SessionSource
        policy = self.service.policy
        self.service.validate_member(row['team'],row['owner'])
        original = SessionSource.from_dict(json.loads(row['original_source']))
        if (original.scope_id!=row['team'] or original.user_id!=row['owner'] or
                not original.thread_id or not await policy.prepare_message(
                    row['owner'],original.chat_id,row['team']) or
                policy.state['conversations'].get(original.chat_id,{}).get('kind')!='shared' or
                not policy.authorize_source(original)):
            raise AccessError('The original Slack thread is no longer available to this requester.',403)
        return original

    async def prepare(self, row):
        await self.validate_destination(row)
        policy = self.service.policy
        profile = 'task-' + row['id']
        await asyncio.to_thread(policy.ensure_profile,profile,
            {'workspace_id':row['team'],'user_id':row['owner'],'kind':'isolated_task','task_id':row['id']})
        await policy.serve_profile(profile)
        return profile

    async def handle_response(self, event, response, runner):
        source = event.source
        revision = getattr(event,'_slack_revision',None)
        if revision and not self.service.policy.adapter._message_edits.current(revision):
            return
        row = self.store.channel_task(source.to_dict())
        if row is None or row['task_state'] in ('cancelled','completed'):
            return
        if row['task_state']=='active':
            self.execution_route(source)
            # The trusted handler already sent the form to the owner's DM.
            # A waiting model reply is not the channel task's final answer.
            waiting = self.store.channel_task_waiting(source.to_dict())
            human_reply = source.message_id==event.message_id
            if (self.store.channel_task_requested_access(source.to_dict(),event.message_id) or
                    waiting and not human_reply):
                return
            if not response.strip():
                raise AccessError('The account task did not produce a result.',409)
            # Capture before optional vault reads and Slack I/O. A failed
            # redaction or publication must retry the answer, never the work.
            event_key = self.event_key(event)
            queued_reply = bool(row['last_inbound_id'] and row['last_inbound_id']!=event_key)
            self.store.save_channel_result(row['id'],response,event_id=event_key,
                                           private=waiting and human_reply,continuing=waiting or queued_reply)
        await self.deliver(row['id'])

    async def deliver(self, task_id):
        lock = self.delivery_locks.setdefault(task_id,asyncio.Lock())
        async with lock:
            row = next((item for item in self.store.pending_channel_results() if item['id']==task_id),None)
            if row is None:
                return
            original = await self.validate_destination(row)
            target = json.loads(row['source']) if row['result_private'] else original.to_dict()
            edits = getattr(self.service.policy.adapter, '_message_edits', None)
            revision = edits.lookup((original.scope_id, original.chat_id, original.user_id,
                                     original.message_id)) if edits and original.message_id else None
            request_version = json.loads(row['original_source']).get('slack_request_version')
            request_digest = json.loads(row['original_source']).get('slack_request_digest')
            if (revision and request_version and str(revision.version) != request_version
                    and revision.digest != request_digest):
                return  # an edit was admitted while this result was waiting for publication
            client = self.service.policy.client()
            client_id = str(uuid5(NAMESPACE_URL,'clanker-channel-result:' + task_id +
                                 (':' + row['result_event_id'] if row['result_event_id'] else '')))
            # Recover a Slack ACK lost before the SQLite completion commit.
            cursor = None
            posted = None
            while True:
                args = {'channel':target['chat_id'],'ts':target['thread_id'],'limit':100}
                if cursor:args['cursor']=cursor
                history = await client.conversations_replies(**args)
                posted = next((m for m in history.get('messages',[]) if m.get('client_msg_id')==client_id),None)
                cursor = history.get('response_metadata',{}).get('next_cursor')
                if posted or not cursor:break
            if posted is None:
                # Cancellation may have happened while waiting for Slack.
                row = next((item for item in self.store.pending_channel_results() if item['id']==task_id),None)
                if row is None:return
                await self.validate_destination(row)
                # Membership refresh awaits Slack. Honor a cancellation that
                # committed during that refresh before beginning publication.
                row = next((item for item in self.store.pending_channel_results() if item['id']==task_id),None)
                if row is None:return
                text = self.store.code_crypto().decrypt(row['result_payload']).decode()
                from agent.vault_store import scrub_secret_from_text
                from agent.redact import redact_registered_vault_values, redact_sensitive_text
                from gateway.run import _profile_runtime_scope
                # Outbox recovery runs outside the turn. Rebuild this owner's
                # contact scrubbing under the worker scope before publication.
                with _profile_runtime_scope(self.home(row)):
                    self.service.personal.register_redactions(SimpleNamespace(source=original))
                    for item in self.service.delegations.items(row['team'],row['owner']):
                        access = self.service.delegations.lookup(row['team'],row['owner'],item['id'])
                        text = scrub_secret_from_text(text,access.secret())
                    text = redact_registered_vault_values(redact_sensitive_text(text,force=True))
                if revision and not edits.current(revision):
                    return
                if revision and revision.reply.ids and row['result_message_ts'] is None and not row['result_private']:
                    result = await edits.update_reply(self.service.policy.adapter, revision, text,
                        {'slack_team_id':original.scope_id,'thread_id':original.thread_id})
                    if not result.success:
                        raise AccessError('The updated channel result remains pending.', 409)
                    posted = {'ts':result.message_id}
                else:
                    posted = await client.chat_postMessage(channel=target['chat_id'],thread_ts=target['thread_id'],
                        text=text,client_msg_id=client_id,unfurl_links=False,unfurl_media=False)
                    if revision and row['result_message_ts'] is None and not row['result_private']:
                        revision.reply.ids.append(posted['ts'])
                        await edits.save(revision)
            self.store.mark_channel_result(task_id,posted['ts'])

    def recover_response(self, row, event_id):
        """Adopt a completed native reply after a coordinator-store crash gap."""
        from hermes_state import SessionDB
        database = SessionDB(db_path=self.home(row)/'state.db')
        try:
            anchor = database._read_one("SELECT id,session_id FROM messages WHERE role='user' "
                "AND platform_message_id=? ORDER BY id DESC LIMIT 1",(event_id,))
            if anchor is None:return None
            tail = database.get_messages(anchor['session_id'],after_id=anchor['id'])
            if not tail or any(message['role']=='user' for message in tail):return None
            final = tail[-1]
            if final['role']=='assistant' and not final.get('tool_calls') and isinstance(final.get('content'),str):
                return final['content']
            return None
        finally:
            database.close()

    async def drain(self):
        for row in self.store.pending_channel_results():
            try:
                await self.deliver(row['id'])
            except Exception:
                # The encrypted outbox retains the exact response for the next pass.
                continue

                if row is None:return

                if row is None:return

                from agent.redact import redact_registered_vault_values, redact_sensitive_text

                with _profile_runtime_scope(self.home(row)):

                    for item in self.service.delegations.items(row['team'],row['owner']):
                        access = self.service.delegations.lookup(row['team'],row['owner'],item['id'])
                        text = scrub_secret_from_text(text,access.secret())

        """Adopt a completed native reply after a coordinator-store crash gap."""

"""Private execution and durable channel replies for authenticated Slack tasks."""
import asyncio

from types import SimpleNamespace

from .store import AccessError


class ChannelTasks:
    def __init__(self, service):
        self.service = service
        self.delivery_locks = {}

    @property
    def store(self):
        return self.service.store

    def home(self, row):
        return self.service.policy.home / 'profiles' / ('task-' + row['id'])

    @staticmethod
    def event_key(event):
        revision = getattr(event,'_slack_revision',None)
        return str(event.message_id) + (':' + str(revision.version) if revision else '')

    def request_context(self, turn):
        row = self.store.channel_task(turn.source.to_dict())
        goal = ('Existing channel task:\n' + row['task'] + '\n\n') if row else ''
        if not turn.conversation:
            return goal + turn.message
        conversation = [{'role': role, 'content': text} for role, text in turn.conversation]
        return (goal + 'Originating channel conversation (context only, not account authorization):\n' +
                json.dumps(conversation, ensure_ascii=False) +
                '\n\nLatest request or clarification answer:\n' + turn.message)

    async def admit_event(self, event):
        source = event.source
        member = self.service.validate_member(source.scope_id,source.user_id)
        private = source.chat_id==member['dm_id'] and source.chat_type=='dm'
        row = self.store.linked_channel_task(source.to_dict(),private=private)
        if row is None:return True
        if private:
            if row['task_state']=='cancelled':return False
            await self.prepare(row)
            if row['task_state']=='result_pending':
                await self.deliver(row['id'])
            if not self.store.begin_channel_reply(row['id'],self.event_key(event)):
                return False
            from agent.gateway_context import IsolatedGatewayTask
            from gateway.session_identity import clear_identity
            clear_identity(source)
            source.profile = 'task-' + row['id']
            source.isolated_task = IsolatedGatewayTask(row['id'],self.handle_response)
            self.execution_route(source)
            context = ('Continue this existing task, preserving confirmed choices and the stopping point. '
                       'Authentication is a step, not completion of the requested task.\n' + row['task'])
        else:
            # Public status is coordinator metadata, never a private worker's
            # messages, account observations, saved identifiers or code values.
            context = 'Linked worker state: ' + row['task_state'] + '. A completed worker turn means its reply was delivered, not that a booking or purchase succeeded.'
            if row['source']:
                form = self.store.channel_form_status(json.loads(row['source']))
                if form:
                    kind,status = form
                    label = 'verification' if kind=='code' else kind
                    context += '\n' + label + ' form: ' + ('submitted' if status in ('saved','resumed') else status) + '.'
                    context += ' Submitted means received by the backend; it does not prove website acceptance or a booking.'
            context += ' Keep credentials and passenger/contact details in the linked private DM. Do not start another handoff for a status check.'
        event.channel_context = '\n\n'.join(part for part in (event.channel_context,context) if part)
        return True

    def execution_route(self, source):
        from agent.gateway_context import isolated_gateway_task
        task = isolated_gateway_task(source)
        row = self.store.channel_task(source.to_dict())
        if (task is None or row is None or task.task_id!=row['id'] or
                row['task_state']!='active' or source.chat_id!=self.service.validate_member(
                    row['team'],row['owner'])['dm_id']):
            raise AccessError('This isolated account task is no longer authorized.',403)
        original = json.loads(row['original_source'])
        policy = self.service.policy
        if (not policy.authorize_sender(row['owner'],original['chat_id']) or
                self.service.private_home(row['team'],row['owner'])!=Path(row['home'])):
            raise AccessError('The original account task is no longer authorized.',403)
        return 'task-' + row['id']

    def restore(self, source):
        """Restore a coordinator resume; native owner replies use admit_event."""
        from agent.gateway_context import IsolatedGatewayTask
        row = self.store.channel_task(source.to_dict())
        if row is None:
            return None
        source.isolated_task = IsolatedGatewayTask(row['id'], self.handle_response)
        return row

    async def validate_destination(self, row):
        from gateway.session import SessionSource
        policy = self.service.policy
        self.service.validate_member(row['team'],row['owner'])
        original = SessionSource.from_dict(json.loads(row['original_source']))
        if (original.scope_id!=row['team'] or original.user_id!=row['owner'] or
                not original.thread_id or not await policy.prepare_message(
                    row['owner'],original.chat_id,row['team']) or
                policy.state['conversations'].get(original.chat_id,{}).get('kind')!='shared' or
                not policy.authorize_source(original)):

        return original

    async def prepare(self, row):

"""Real Slack intake and durable task routing; transport and model are fixtures."""
import asyncio
import json
from types import SimpleNamespace
from unittest.mock import AsyncMock

import pytest

from test_clanker_channel_tasks import workspace, provision, channel_turn, settle, worker_turn
from agent.gateway_context import isolated_gateway_task
from agent.vault_store import VaultStore
from gateway.config import Platform, PlatformConfig
from gateway.run import GatewayRunner
from gateway.session import build_session_key
from plugins.platforms.slack.adapter import SlackAdapter
from vault.service import VaultService


def native_intake(workspace):
    adapter = SlackAdapter(PlatformConfig(enabled=True, token='xoxb-fixture',
        typing_indicator=False, extra={'reactions': False}))
    runner = object.__new__(GatewayRunner)
    runner.config = SimpleNamespace(multiplex_profiles=True, profile_routes=[])
    runner._served_profile_homes = workspace.runner._served_profile_homes
    runner.adapters = {Platform.SLACK: adapter}
    adapter.gateway_runner = runner
    adapter._team_clients = {'TT': workspace.client}
    adapter._team_bot_user_ids = {'TT': 'UBOT'}
    adapter._bot_user_id = 'UBOT'
    adapter._workspace_membership = workspace.policy
    adapter._resolve_user_name = AsyncMock(return_value='Fixture member')
    adapter._resolve_channel_name = AsyncMock(return_value='Fixture conversation')
    adapter._hydrate_thread_context = AsyncMock(return_value=(None, [], []))
    adapter._set_assistant_thread_title = AsyncMock()
    workspace.client.conversations_info.side_effect = lambda channel: {'channel':
        {'is_im': True, 'user': channel[1:]} if channel.startswith('D') else {'is_member': True}}
    captured = []
    async def dispatch(a, event, revision, **kwargs):
        a._canonicalize(event.source)
        assert workspace.policy.authorize_source(event.source)
        captured.append(event)
    adapter._message_edits.dispatch = dispatch
    workspace.policy.adapter = adapter
    return adapter, captured


async def intake(workspace, adapter, owner, chat, thread, ts, text):
    workspace.client.conversations_info.return_value = {'channel':
        {'is_im': True, 'user': owner} if chat.startswith('D') else {'is_member': True}}
    await adapter._handle_slack_message({'type': 'message', 'user': owner,
        'channel': chat, 'channel_type': 'im' if chat.startswith('D') else 'channel',
        'team': 'TT', 'ts': ts, 'thread_ts': thread, 'text': text,
        'client_msg_id': 'human-' + ts})


@pytest.mark.asyncio
async def test_native_dm_replies_keep_flight_worker_after_restart_and_deliver_each_turn(workspace):
    await provision(workspace)
    selected = 'Nagpur to Mumbai on 9 October, one adult, AI-2584 at 10:10 PM, accepted INR 6540.'
    events = []
    for index, owner in enumerate(('UA', 'UB', 'UA')):
        turn = channel_turn(workspace, owner=owner, task='yeah', thread='200.' + str(index),
                            message_id='300.' + str(index))
        turn.conversation = (('user', selected), ('assistant', 'Continue the selected booking privately.'))
        await workspace.service.move_private(turn)
        await settle(workspace.service)
        initial = workspace.events[-1]
        await workspace.service.channel_tasks.handle_response(initial, 'Signed in; passenger details are still needed.', workspace.runner)
        events.append(initial)
    restored = VaultService(workspace.policy, workspace.service.config)
    workspace.policy.vault_service = restored
    workspace.service = restored
    adapter, captured = native_intake(workspace)
    for index, initial in enumerate(events):
        owner = initial.source.user_id
        before = len(captured)
        await intake(workspace, adapter, owner, initial.source.chat_id, initial.source.thread_id,
                     '400.' + str(index), 'go further now')
        assert len(captured) == before + 1
        reply = captured[-1]
        assert reply.source.profile == initial.source.profile
        assert isolated_gateway_task(reply.source).task_id == isolated_gateway_task(initial.source).task_id
        assert build_session_key(reply.source, profile=reply.source.profile) == build_session_key(initial.source, profile=initial.source.profile)
        assert selected in reply.channel_context and 'go further now' == reply.text
        await intake(workspace, adapter, owner, initial.source.chat_id, initial.source.thread_id,
                     '401.' + str(index), 'keep that selected flight')
        queued = captured[-1]
        result = 'The selected flight is ready for passenger details, task ' + str(index)
        await restored.channel_tasks.handle_response(reply, result, adapter.gateway_runner)
        assert restored.store.channel_task(queued.source.to_dict())['task_state']=='active'
        await restored.channel_tasks.handle_response(queued, 'Selected flight retained.', adapter.gateway_runner)
        posted = [m for m in workspace.messages if m['channel'] == 'CSHARED' and m.get('thread_ts') == '200.' + str(index)]
        assert [m['text'] for m in posted] == ['Signed in; passenger details are still needed.', result, 'Selected flight retained.']
        assert len({m['client_msg_id'] for m in posted}) == 3
        # A duplicate intake after another restart cannot reopen a delivered turn.
        restored = VaultService(workspace.policy, restored.config)
        workspace.policy.vault_service = restored
        workspace.service = restored
        adapter, captured = native_intake(workspace)
        await intake(workspace, adapter, owner, initial.source.chat_id, initial.source.thread_id,
                     '401.' + str(index), 'keep that selected flight')
        assert captured == []
    # Another owner cannot adopt the private worker by quoting its DM thread.
    await intake(workspace, adapter, 'UB', 'DUB', events[0].source.thread_id, '500.1', 'continue')
    assert captured[-1].source.profile == workspace.policy.state['members']['UB']['profile']
    assert isolated_gateway_task(captured[-1].source) is None


@pytest.mark.asyncio
async def test_code_waiting_reply_and_public_status_share_one_task_without_false_delivery(workspace):
    await provision(workspace)
    workspace.client.chat_getPermalink = AsyncMock(side_effect=lambda channel,message_ts:
        {'permalink':'https://slack.invalid/archives/' + channel + '/p' + message_ts.replace('.','')})
    turn = channel_turn(workspace, task='Continue selected AI-2584 flight', message_id='200.2')
    moved = await workspace.service.move_private(turn)
    assert moved['private_thread_url'].startswith('https://slack.invalid/archives/DUA/')
    await settle(workspace.service)
    initial = workspace.events[-1]
    owner_home = workspace.service.private_home('TT', 'UA')
    meta = VaultStore(owner_home / 'vault').add_item('login', 'Fixture flights',
        {'identifier': 'fixture@example.invalid', 'identifier_type': 'email', 'password': 'REDACTED'},
        origin='https://flights.invalid')
    form = await workspace.service.request_code(worker_turn(workspace, initial), meta)
    adapter, captured = native_intake(workspace)
    await intake(workspace, adapter, 'UA', 'DUA', initial.source.thread_id, '600.1', 'we good now?')
    reply = captured[-1]
    assert reply.source.profile == initial.source.profile
    await workspace.service.channel_tasks.handle_response(reply, 'Your verification form is still waiting.', adapter.gateway_runner)
    assert workspace.messages[-1]['channel'] == 'DUA'
    assert workspace.messages[-1]['thread_ts'] == initial.source.thread_id
    assert workspace.service.store.channel_task(reply.source.to_dict())['task_state'] == 'active'
    assert not any(m['channel'] == 'CSHARED' for m in workspace.messages)
    await intake(workspace, adapter, 'UA', 'CSHARED', '200.1', '600.2', '<@UBOT> sent the code')
    public = captured[-1]
    assert isolated_gateway_task(public.source) is None
    assert 'verification form: waiting' in public.channel_context
    workspace.client.conversations_info.return_value = {'channel': {'is_member': True}}
    again = await workspace.service.move_private(channel_turn(workspace, task='sent the code', message_id='600.2'))
    assert again['private_thread_url']==moved['private_thread_url']
    await settle(workspace.service)
    with workspace.service.store.connection() as db:
        assert db.execute('SELECT count(*) FROM transfers').fetchone()[0] == 1
